Accepted.description: The one answer sign-up, resend and forgot-password give, whatever the address.
Accepted.title: Accepted

AdminUserPatch.description: Only the fields present are changed. `hours_cap_seconds: null` clears the override.
AdminUserPatch.title: AdminUserPatch

CalendarOut.description:
The calendar settings page's whole state. `state` is for choosing what to draw
(`not_connected` shows the Connect button; `connected` and `degraded` show the connected card;
`needs_reconnect` shows it with a Connect again button); `state_text` is the sentence for it.
`connected` is true while the calendar can still be read (`connected` or `degraded`).
`account_email` is the account that was connected (shown as the connected address), and
`provider` which calendar it is (`google` or `microsoft`); both are null when none is.
`last_sync_at` is the last time the calendar was read in full, null before the first sync.
`last_error` is the last failure in plain words, null when the last attempt worked.
`rule` is the person's auto-join rule (`all`, `organizer` or `none`; `all` until they choose)
and `rule_text` its label ("Joining all meetings"). `calendar_template_id` is the person's own
template chosen for calendar meetings, null for the default (their first, oldest, template).
`auto_join_paused` is true while the operator has stopped calendar auto-join for everyone
(`AUTOJOIN_ENABLED=false`): the rows still show what the rule says, but no bot is sent, and
`auto_join_paused_text` is the line to show (null when it is not paused).
`upcoming` is empty unless connected.
CalendarOut.title: CalendarOut

ConnectIn.description:
`features` are what to ask Google for: `calendar` (read events, to decide which meetings
to join) and/or `meet` (learn that a Meet call you host began). `return_to` is a relative
path to land on afterwards; anything else becomes `/settings`.
ConnectIn.title: ConnectIn

ConnectOut.description:
`authorize_url` is where to send the browser (navigate to it; do not fetch it).
`show_unverified_notice` is true until Google has verified the app: show the "Google hasn't
verified this app" explainer first.
ConnectOut.title: ConnectOut

DisconnectOut.description:
`status` is always `disconnected`: the call is safe to repeat, and also answers 200 when
nothing was connected. `revoked` is false when Google could not be asked to remove the access
(it was unreachable, or the stored key could not be read): the data is deleted here
regardless, but tell the person to also remove Beyric at myaccount.google.com/permissions.
It is true when Google confirmed, and also when there was nothing left to revoke (a repeat
cannot re-check an earlier failure: act on the first answer).
DisconnectOut.title: DisconnectOut

EmailPreferencesIn.description:
`notify_email` must be a JSON boolean (the string "false" is refused) and nothing else may
be sent: this body cannot change any other setting.
EmailPreferencesIn.title: EmailPreferencesIn

EmailPreferencesOut.description:
`notify_email`: whether the owner of a meeting is emailed when its notes are ready. On
unless it was turned off. Sign-in mail (verification, password reset) is not affected.
EmailPreferencesOut.title: EmailPreferencesOut

InvitePreview.description: What an invitation link says, for the page that opens it (public: the token is the key).
InvitePreview.title: InvitePreview

MeetingMilestones.description:
What a meeting's page shows: dates proposed from it ("Set milestone: <name>, <date>?") and
the ones already confirmed.
MeetingMilestones.title: MeetingMilestones

MilestoneLine.description: The one milestone line a project shows.
MilestoneLine.title: MilestoneLine

OverrideIn.description:
The person's switch for one meeting: true joins it, false does not, null clears the switch
so the rule decides again. The field is required (null must be sent on purpose).
OverrideIn.title: OverrideIn

PersonOut.description: A member of the caller's team who can be given a task.
PersonOut.title: PersonOut

ProjectPatch.description: A partial change: send only what changes (the screen saves one field at a time).
ProjectPatch.title: ProjectPatch

RecurringOut.description:
The cards, soonest next occurrence first; empty when no calendar is connected or it holds no
recurring meeting (draw nothing then). `timezone` is the zone the texts are written in.
RecurringOut.title: RecurringOut

RecurringSeries.description:
One recurring meeting. `name` is the event's title; `cadence` is `Daily, 14:00`,
`Weekly on Mondays, 14:00` (several days: `Mondays and Wednesdays`) or just `Recurring` when
the stored times do not prove more. `next_starts_at` is the next occurrence that has not
started, and `next_text` the same moment in the asked-for zone as `Mon 9 Nov, 14:00`. Show the
texts as they are. No attendees, link, passcode or source id is carried.
RecurringSeries.title: RecurringSeries

SettingsIn.description:
What to change; a field that is left out stays as it is. `rule` is `all` (every event with
a video link), `organizer` (only meetings the person organises) or `none` (only the meetings
they switch on). Changing it also clears their per-meeting switches on events that have not
started, and re-decides every event from the new rule. `calendar_template_id` is one of the
person's own templates, or null for the default; it also reaches the meetings already planned
that have not sent a bot. At least one field is needed.
SettingsIn.title: SettingsIn

TaskPatch.description:
A partial change: send only the fields that change. A field you leave out is untouched;
`assignee_user_id` and `due_date` set to null clear them.
TaskPatch.title: TaskPatch

TeamMemberPatch.description:
Change a role (owner only) and/or the aliases (an owner or admin, or the person themselves).
Aliases replace the whole list.
TeamMemberPatch.title: TeamMemberPatch

TranslationBrief.description: What the meeting page needs to know about a translation without fetching it.
TranslationBrief.title: TranslationBrief

UpcomingEvent.description:
One synced event in the next seven days. Only what a person needs to recognise it: no
attendees, description, location or meeting link (a Zoom link can carry a passcode).
`will_join_text` is the short answer in words and `reason_text` the sentence behind a no: show
both as they are.

platform_label.description: Google Meet, Zoom or Microsoft Teams; or null
platform_label.title: Platform Label

UpcomingEvent.title: UpcomingEvent

info.description:
Owner-only JSON API for the Beyric Note Taker frontend. Same origin as the app.

Auth is the signed `session` cookie. Call `GET /api/session` first: it returns `csrf_token`,
which every call other than GET must send in the `X-CSRF-Token` header. Every error has the
shape `{"error": {"code", "message"}}` (validation errors add `fields`).
info.title: Beyric Note Taker API

get.description: The most recent mail that could not be sent (never with its link).

put.description:
Open or close sign-up, set the number of accounts (`null` = no limit), the default recorded
hours per account in seconds (`null` = no cap) and whether password sign-up is on. Every field
is required.

get.description: Accounts with their recorded hours, newest first. Accounts being deleted are not listed.

delete.description:
Delete an account and everything of theirs. The user is signed out and their slot is free
at once; the worker then removes their data (bots stopped, recordings deleted at Vexa and
here). The hours ledger keeps seconds only. 409 `last_admin`.

patch.description:
Suspend or reactivate an account (`status`) and set or clear one user's hours override
(`hours_cap_seconds`). Only the fields sent change. A suspended user is signed out on their
next request. 409 `last_admin`: the only active admin cannot be suspended.

post.description:
A one-time password-reset link (30 minutes) for the admin to give the person, for when
mail is not working. Shown once, never mailed; replaces any earlier reset link and tells the
user in the app. Not for admin accounts. 409 `admin_account`, `user_not_verified` or
`account_suspended`.

get.description:
The waiting list, oldest first, without the people removed. `before_id` is the id to
continue after (the last `next_before_id`).

delete.description: Take someone off the list. A live invitation is cancelled and its place freed.

post.description:
Reserve a place for this person for 7 days and invite them. With mail working the link
is emailed (`emailed: true`, `invite_url: null`); without it `invite_url` is returned for the
admin to send. Inviting again replaces the earlier link. 409 `pilot_full` when no place is
free, `waitlist_entry_closed` for someone who joined or was removed.

get.description:
Where Google sends the browser back. Public (checked by the single-use `state` and the
`google_flow` cookie of the browser that started the flow). Always a redirect, never JSON:
success goes to the stored `return_to` with a new session; a failure goes to
`/login?error=<code>` with `google_denied`, `google_failed`, `terms_required`,
`account_suspended`, `pilot_closed` or `email_unsupported`; a full pilot goes to
`/pilot-full` and sets a 15-minute cookie that `GET /api/pilot` reads as `prefill_email`
(the address is never put in a URL).

Send the browser to Google's consent screen (scopes `openid email profile` only). Public;
navigate to it, do not fetch it. `accept_terms=true` must be sent by the sign-up screen: it
is what lets a NEW account be created (an existing one signs in without it). `return_to` is
a relative path to land on afterwards; anything else becomes `/`. 404
`google_signin_unavailable` when the server has no Google client configured.

Everything the calendar settings page shows, in one read (no CSRF header needed): whether
Google Calendar is connected, which Google address, the last time it was read, the last
failure in plain words, and the next seven days of synced events, each with whether the bot
will join it and why not when it will not. Nothing is fetched from Google here: this reads what
the sync job last stored. 404 `calendar_unavailable` while the calendar features are off.

put.description:
The person's switch for one meeting on the Upcoming list (CSRF header needed): `true` joins
it, `false` does not, `null` clears the switch so the rule decides again. The switch beats the
rule in both directions; the stored join is made, revived or cancelled to match, which is what
the runner reads. Answers with the event's new row. 404 `not_found` for an event that is not
the caller's (also after disconnecting); 409 `not_joinable` for an event nothing the person
switches can change (declined, over, cancelled, all day, no meeting link, or Microsoft Teams
before Teams can be joined): `message` is the reason in plain words, and nothing is stored.
404 `calendar_unavailable` while the calendar features are off.

get.description:
The Recurring cards of the Meetings screen (no CSRF header needed): each recurring meeting
on the connected calendar with a cadence worked out from its stored times, and its next
occurrence. `tz` is the viewer's zone (the browser's `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().
timeZone`); without it the texts are in UTC, and the answer says which zone it used. Empty
when no calendar is connected or nothing recurs. Nothing is fetched from Google. 404
`calendar_unavailable` while the calendar features are off, 422 `invalid_timezone` for a zone
name that is not known.

put.description:
Change the auto-join rule and/or the template for calendar meetings (CSRF header needed);
a field left out stays as it is. Answers with the whole state, as `GET /api/calendar` does, so
the page can redraw from it. A changed `rule` clears the person's per-meeting switches on events
that have not started, then decides every stored event again from the new rule: joins it now
forbids are cancelled and joins it now allows are made or revived (the same rules the sync
applies; nothing is fetched from Google and no bot is sent here). Choosing the rule that is
already set changes nothing. 404 `not_found` for a template that is not the caller's own,
404 `calendar_unavailable` while the calendar features are off.

get.description:
Where Google sends the browser back after the consent screen. Public in the guard (it
answers a signed-out visitor itself) but checked by the single-use `state`, the signed-in
user the flow was started for, and the `calendar_flow` cookie. Always a redirect, never JSON:
success goes to the stored `return_to` with `?calendar=connected`; a failure goes there with
`?calendar_error=` `google_denied`, `google_failed`, `scope_missing` (the calendar box was
unticked), `no_refresh_token`, `wrong_account` or `already_connected` (another provider's
calendar is connected); nobody signed in goes to
`/login?error=google_failed`. 404 `calendar_unavailable` while the feature is off.

post.description:
Start connecting Google Calendar (CSRF header needed). Returns the Google consent URL to
navigate to. Only the permissions in `features` are asked for, each at the moment its feature
is switched on; permissions given earlier are kept. Sets the `calendar_flow` cookie that ties
the callback to this browser. 404 `calendar_unavailable` when the calendar features are off,
409 `calendar_already_connected` when another provider's calendar is connected (one calendar at
a time), 503 `calendar_unavailable` when the server cannot store a token safely. `provider` is
`google`; `microsoft` answers 404 `calendar_unavailable` until it is built.

Disconnect the caller's Google account (CSRF header needed, no body). Revokes the access at
Google, then deletes the caller's calendar events, all their scheduled joins (every state) and
calendar notifications, and the stored token. Meetings already recorded, the hours used and
the settings stay; a meeting being recorded right now carries on. Safe to repeat (200 again),
and it works while the calendar features are switched off. If Google cannot be reached the
local deletion still happens and `revoked` is false: tell the person to remove Beyric at
myaccount.google.com/permissions.
Afterwards `connect` works again, for the same or another Google account.

get.description:
Everything the caller's meetings decided, newest meeting first, grouped by meeting. `q`
matches a decision's words or its meeting's title (a title match shows all of that meeting's
decisions). `limit` counts meetings, not decisions. For the next page pass `before_id` =
`next_before_id`. A decision the caller hid is not listed.

post.description:
Remove a decision from the log. It is hidden, never edited, and stays hidden when the
meeting's notes are rewritten. Hiding it again is 204 too.

get.description:
The caller's meetings, plus any shared with their team, newest first. For the next page
pass `before_id` = `next_before_id`.

post.description:
Send the bot to a Google Meet or Zoom link, through the same placement as every other way a
bot is sent. 403 `hours_cap_reached` once the account has used its recorded hours. 409 for the
rest: `user_limit` (the account is at the most bots allowed at once), `already_in_meeting` (a
bot of the account's is already in that meeting), `meeting_has_note_taker` (another account's
bot is in that meeting; the text names nobody) and `bot_busy` (the note taker is full, or a
placement is under way; the text never says whose meeting holds it). 502 `bot_send_failed`
when the bot host did not take the bot.

delete.description:
Delete a meeting and everything taken from it: transcript, notes, translations, decisions,
open questions, review items, notifications, mail still waiting to be sent, the audio and
Vexa's copy of it. The recorded hours stay counted. Only the one who recorded it (a teammate
or anyone else gets 404). 409 `meeting_active` while the bot is in the call or the notes are
being written, 409 `meeting_busy` when the worker holds it (try again), 502
`recording_delete_failed` when Vexa would not remove the recording: nothing is deleted.

post.description:
Take the bot out of a meeting that is still `bot_sent` and discard it. Only when `can_cancel`
is true: once the bot has been ended with `POST /end` (the notes are being written) it is 409
`already_ending`, and while the bot is still starting (its send got no clear answer; the page
reads "Starting the bot") it is 409 `bot_starting`: try again in a minute; 409 `meeting_busy`
when the worker holds the meeting, try again.

"End now and write the notes": take the bot out of the call and write the notes from what
it recorded. Only when `can_end` is true (409 `not_endable` otherwise, 409 `already_ending`
when it was asked already, 409 `meeting_busy` when the worker holds the meeting: try again).
The meeting stays `bot_sent` while the bot leaves, then follows the usual steps; it is not a
cancel and nothing is discarded.

get.description:
The notes (and, with `transcript=true`, the full transcript) as a PDF or Word file.

`language` `fr` or `es` builds it from the finished, current translation (409
`translation_missing` when there is none: translate first); `en`, the default, is the
original.

Built when asked and never stored. One file is built at a time per server process: a second
request meanwhile gets 503 `export_busy` with `Retry-After`. The file name is the meeting's
title, cleaned, in `Content-Disposition`.

200.description: The file. Built for this request and not stored.

404.description: No such meeting (or not one the caller may read)

409.description: `not_ready`: the notes are not written yet; `translation_missing`: no finished, current translation in that language

500.description: `export_failed`: the file could not be built

get.description:
The dates proposed from this meeting and the milestones already set from it, for its page.
Anyone who can read the meeting may ask; `can_confirm` says whether the caller may confirm.

post.description: Rewrite the notes of a `ready` meeting with a template. Runs in the request: allow 5 min.

Resume a failed meeting at the step that failed. Only when `can_retry` is true. For a
meeting whose join the worker ended (Google refused the bot, or it hung on a prompt) this
sends a new bot instead, no sooner than 5 minutes after the failure.

delete.description:
Make the meeting private again: teammates lose it at once. Only the owner; 404 for anyone
else. Doing it twice is fine.

404.description: No such meeting (or not the caller's)

post.description:
Share the meeting with the caller's team (the "Share with team" switch): teammates may read
its notes, transcript and tasks, never change it. Only the one who recorded it (a teammate or
anyone else gets 404). Doing it twice is fine. The team's default (`share_new_meetings`) is
read once, when the notes are first written; this is how a person shares one by hand.

404.description: No such meeting (or not the caller's)

get.description:
A meeting's action items as tasks, for its page ("8 tasks created, assigned to 3 people").
Anyone who can read the meeting may ask.

post.description:
Read the tasks out of an older meeting's notes ("Extract tasks from this meeting"). Owner
only. 409 `extraction_pending` while the meeting is already being read, 409 `tasks_off` when
the owner has switched tasks off. The tasks it makes are not New and nobody is emailed.

Translate the notes and transcript of a ready meeting into French or Spanish. 200 with the
translation when one is already cached for the current text; otherwise 202 with
`status: "translating"` and the work is queued. A failed or stale translation asked for again
is queued again. Asking again while it is being made changes nothing.

200.description: A finished translation of the current text, from the cache.

202.description: Queued, or already being made: ask again every 2 seconds.

404.description: No such meeting (or not the caller's)

409.description: `not_ready`: the notes are not written yet

delete.description:
Throw the translation away so it can be made again (also cancels one still queued). It does
not give back one of the day's 20.

get.description:
The translation in one language: its `status` (poll every 2 seconds while `translating`),
and when `ready` the `notes`, `notes_html` and `transcript`. 404 `no_translation` when none
was asked for, or for a language that is not offered.

The team's confirmed milestones, soonest first, with how many tasks are filed under each
and how many are done (over the tasks the caller may see). Proposals are not listed here:
they live on the meeting they came from (`GET /api/meetings/{id}/milestones`).

post.description: Make a milestone by hand (owner or admin). It is confirmed at once.

delete.description:
Delete a milestone, or turn a proposal down (owner or admin). Tasks filed under it stay,
with no milestone.

patch.description: Rename, move to another date or another project (owner or admin).

post.description:
Turn a proposal into a milestone ("Set milestone: Client Portal launch, 8 Dec?" then
Confirm). Owner or admin. Confirming one that is already confirmed changes nothing. Send a
`project_id` to choose the project; left out, the one it was filed under stays.

get.description:
The caller's notifications, newest first. For the next page pass `before_id` =
`next_before_id`.

post.description: Mark all of the caller's notifications read.

Mark one notification read (repeating it keeps the first read time). 404 for someone
else's.

Mail a password-reset link (valid 30 minutes) if the address has a confirmed account.
Public. Always 202 with the same body: it never says whether the address has an account.

Choose a new password with the token from the reset mail. Public. Signs that user out
everywhere and does not sign them in. 400 `token_invalid_or_expired`; 422
`password_too_weak` leaves the token usable.

get.description:
Whether sign-up is `open`, `full` or `closed`. Public. No counts of other people.

`prefill_email` is the Google address of a visitor just turned away by `pilot_full` (a signed
15-minute cookie), so the waitlist form can start filled in. `google_signin` says whether the
Google button should be shown.

The team's projects, oldest first. Every member reads them. `open_tasks` counts only the
open tasks the caller may see.

post.description:
Make a project (owner or admin). A blank name is allowed: the screen opens a blank project
and saves the name as it is typed.

delete.description:
Delete a project (owner or admin). Its tasks stay and now have no project; its milestones
go with it.

patch.description:
Change the name, colour or keywords (owner or admin). The screen sends one field per
change, debounced; a field left out is untouched. `keywords` replaces the whole list.

get.description:
The caller's "Please check" items from their meetings: `state=open` (default) or
`checked`. Newest meeting first, in the order of the notes.

post.description: Mark an item checked. Checking it again keeps the first time.
Put a checked item back among the open ones.

Add the corrected spelling to the caller's vocabulary and mark the item checked. 400
`invalid_term` (nothing changes). 409 `duplicate_term` when the term is already there; the
item is still marked checked. The notes of this meeting are not rewritten: offer "rewrite
the notes" (`POST /meetings/{id}/regenerate`) afterwards.

delete.description:
Log this user out everywhere: every session cookie they were issued stops working.
Other users are not affected.

get.description:
Whether the cookie is a logged-in session, plus the CSRF token to send on writes.

Public. Call it first: it also gives a logged-out visitor a cookie to log in with. Logged in,
it names the user and reports their recorded hours (`usage`).

post.description:
Log in with email and password. Public, but needs the X-CSRF-Token from `GET /session`.

401 `invalid_credentials` for a wrong password or an unknown email (the same answer for
both, and for an account whose email was never confirmed). 403 `account_suspended` when the
password was right but the account is suspended. The login limits are the page's: 5 failed
attempts per client address in 5 minutes and 10 per email in an hour, then 429. The response
carries the new session's CSRF token: it replaces the one from before login.

get.description:
Whether the caller is emailed when the notes of their meeting are ready (on by default,
also for an account that has no settings row yet).

put.description:
Turn the notes-ready email on or off for the caller. The mail is checked against this
setting when it is sent, so turning it off also stops one already queued.

get.description:
The language meetings open in when a translation exists: `en` (the original, the default,
also for an account that has no settings row yet), `fr` or `es`.

put.description:
Set the default notes language. Nothing is translated by this: a meeting opens in it only
when that translation already exists, otherwise it opens in the original with an offer.

get.description:
The two switches of Settings > Tasks (both on by default, also for an account with no
settings row yet).

put.description:
Set both switches. They are read when a meeting is read (tasks) and when the mail is sent
(assignees), so turning email off also stops mail already queued.

get.description:
The zone meeting times, due dates and reminder mails are written in. `UTC` with `is_set`
false until the person chooses one.

put.description: Set the caller's time zone (a name from the IANA database, e.g. `Africa/Lagos`).

post.description:
Create an account with a password. Public (needs the X-CSRF-Token).

Answers 202 `check_your_email` for a new address AND for one that already has an account (a
verified one gets a "you already have an account" mail), so it cannot be used to find out who
is registered. The account cannot sign in until the emailed link is confirmed. Errors that do
not depend on the address: 403 `pilot_closed`, 409 `pilot_full`, 403
`password_signup_disabled`, 400 `invite_invalid`, 422 `password_too_weak`, `invalid_email`,
`invalid_name`, `terms_required`, 429 `too_many_requests` (5 sign-ups per hour per address)
and `server_busy`. `accept_terms` must be true: the account records the version accepted.
A second sign-up for the same address within a minute is answered 202 and does nothing.

Mail a new verification link to an unconfirmed account. Public. Always 202, whatever the
address and whether or not a mail was sent: one per minute per email and 5 per hour per
client address are sent, the rest are dropped silently.

get.description:
The sprints of the board: up to 20 closed ones, the current and the next. With no
`project` it is the team's series, counting the tasks of every project; with a project it is
that project's series (its own when it has a sprint length of its own, else the team's)
counting that project's tasks. The first call for a team makes its first two sprints.

post.description:
Close the current sprint now (owner or admin). Its unfinished tasks move to the next
sprint and are marked carried over; the next sprint starts today (its end date does not
change) and a new next is made. 409 `sprint_not_current` for a sprint that is closed or is
still the next one.

get.description:
The tasks the caller can see: those assigned to them, those from meetings they can read,
and their team's manual tasks. Newest first; for the next page pass `before_id` =
`next_before_id`. `attention` counts every open task the caller sees, whatever the filter.

post.description: Make a task by hand, in the caller's team. Anyone on the team may. It has no meeting.

delete.description:
Delete a task. Owners and admins may delete any task they can see; a member only the tasks
they made. An AI task deleted here does not come back when the notes are read again.

patch.description:
Change some fields of a task. Owners and admins may change anything. A member may change
the status and due date of a task assigned to them, take a task that has no owner (set
`assignee_user_id` to themselves), and change everything about a task they made; anything
more is 403 `team_forbidden` and nothing is changed. A status change clears "New".

get.description:
The caller's team: its name, the sharing default, the caller's role and what that role may
do. Every account has one (a team of one until it joins another).

patch.description:
Rename the team, switch "Share new meetings" and/or set the sprint length, custom days and
Monday to Friday switch (owner or admin; 422 `align_needs_week5` for the switch on any other
length). Changing a sprint setting redraws the open sprints. The default applies,
when a meeting's notes are first written, to meetings of the team's owner and admins only; a
member's meetings are never shared by it. 403 `team_forbidden`.

post.description:
Invite up to 10 people by email (owner or admin; only the owner may invite an admin). One
mail each, a link that works once for 7 days. A new person's invitation reserves one of the
pilot's places (409 `pilot_full` when there is none) and bypasses a closed or full pilot for
that address. Answers per address: `sent`, `resent` (already invited: a new link went out),
`already_member`, `already_invited` (one went out a minute ago), `invalid_email`. The answer
is the same for an address with an account and one without (except `pilot_full`, which only
an address needing a place can get). 409 `invite_limit`: 10 open invitations or 20 a day per
team.

Join the team of an invitation link, signed in with the account the invitation was sent to
(the same answer for a wrong, used, expired, revoked or someone else's link). Your team of one
is dissolved: your tasks move to the team you join; your meetings stay yours and private. 409
`already_on_team` when you are on a team with other people: leave it first. A new person does
not call this: signing up with the link joins them when their email is confirmed.

get.description:
What an invitation link is for, so the page can say "Dan invited you to join Product team"
and send the visitor to sign in (`has_account`) or sign up with the link. Public: the token in
the query is the credential, and it reveals nothing to anyone who does not hold it. 400
`invite_invalid` for a wrong, used, expired or revoked link: one answer for all of them.

delete.description: Cancel an invitation: its link stops working and its place is free again.

post.description:
Send an open (or expired) invitation again: a new link, the old one stops working, 7 more
days. 429 `too_soon` within a minute of the last mail; 409 `pilot_full` for an expired
invitation to a new person when the pilot has filled up meanwhile.

get.description:
The people on the team, and (for everyone) the invitations still open. Each member carries
what the caller may do to them, so the screen shows only buttons that work.

delete.description:
Remove a member, or leave the team (your own id). They get a fresh team of one; the open
tasks assigned to them become unassigned; their meetings stay theirs and are unshared. An owner
or admin removes members; only the owner removes an admin; the owner cannot be removed and
cannot leave while others remain (409 `owner_cannot_leave`). 403 `team_forbidden`.

patch.description:
Change a member's role (owner only; `admin` or `member`) and/or the names they are matched
by in meetings (`aliases`, replacing the list: an owner or admin for anyone, a member for
themselves). All of it is refused if any part is not allowed (403 `team_forbidden`).

get.description: The caller's templates, sorted by name.

delete.description:
Delete a template. Meetings written with it keep their notes and the template name they
show; the calendar setting that pointed at it moves to the oldest template left. 409
`last_template` for the only one.

post.description:
Confirm an email with the token from the link and the password chosen at sign-up.
Public. The page the link opens must show a password field and a button that calls this
(mail scanners open links, and a GET must not verify). Does not sign the user in.
400 `token_invalid_or_expired`: wrong, used or older than 24 hours. 400 `password_mismatch`:
not the password submitted with this link's sign-up; the link stays usable until 5 wrong
passwords, after which it answers `token_invalid_or_expired`.

get.description: The caller's terms, sorted alphabetically.

post.description:
Leave an email (and optionally a name) for when a place opens. Public. Always 202
`on_the_list`, whether or not the address is already listed or has an account; a repeat
changes nothing, and 5 per hour per address and 1 per minute per email are dropped silently.
422 `invalid_email` for a malformed address.
